newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends below 8,000 points on signs of stronger growth.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends below 8,000 points on signs of stronger growth.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average staggered lower Tuesday, ending below 8,000 points for the first time in three weeks on new evidence that economic growth is accelerating from its tame second quarter pace.
The Dow was off 101.27 points, or 1.2 percent, at 7,960.84, its first close below the 8,000 level since July 21, when the blue chip average ended at 7,906.72.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,549 to 1,252 on moderate volume of 499 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The economic news, which came in the form of a stronger than expected weekly report on the nation's retail sales, dealt a severe blow to the already jittery bond market, which is bracing for a critical monthly retail sales report Wednesday.
The Redbook retail sales index showed seasonally adjusted retail sales rose a robust 0.9 percent in the week ended Aug. 9.

"People are aware of the potency of (tomorrow's) retail sales number," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "If there's one thing that's going to change the Fed's mind, it's a couple of months of buoyant retail sales."

In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond slumped 13/32, or $4.06 on a $1,000 bond, and the yield jumped to 6.67 percent from 6.64 percent at Monday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
"If there's any sign the consumer is really starting to spend, that will push the whole inflation issue right back to the forefront," said Wachtel.
Investors were also edgy ahead of Wednesday's producer price index for July, and there was concern that the inflation gauge may rise after falling for six straight months.
"To dismiss PPI out of hand would be a mistake," said Pat Alexander, head trader at BancAmerica Securities. "But retail sales is clearly what the market is more focused on."

According to a Reuters survey, retail sales were expected to have risen 0.7 percent and sales excluding autos were seen up 0.5 percent in July, after rising 0.5 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively, in June.
The government will also report Thursday on inflation at the consumer level for July.
With stocks still richly valued and investors back on their heels, analysts predicted more volatility for the near term.
"We're in a nervous environment, and volatility is a fact of life here," said James Crawford, senior vice president at Trevor Stewart Burton & Jacobsen Inc.

Federal Reserve policy-makers meet Aug. 19 to consider their next move on interest rates. They raised short-term rates in March, the first increase in more than two years to ward off inflation, but have held them steady since.
"I wouldn't be surprised by a period of consolidation here, and ultimately I think it's probably going to prove to be beneficial over the long term," Crawford said.
Among individual issues, Amgen Inc. fell 6-15/16 to 50-3/16 after the biotechnology company warned of reduced earnings from its drug Epogen due to changes in Medicaid reimbursement policies.
U.S. listed shares in Chinese companies were strong, lifted by hopes that China's upcoming Communist Party Congress would result in industry restructurings, which would improve earnings outlooks.

Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical Co. jumped 3-5/8 to 17-1/2, Shanghai Petrochemical Co. climbed 4-1/16 to 39-3/16 and Jilin Chemical Industrial Co. added 3-1/16 to 28-13/16. All three ranked among the top gainers in point terms on the NYSE.
The Nasdaq Composite index skidded 10.50 points to 1,576.24, its fourth straight losing session.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 10.47 to 926.53. The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.12 at 643.23.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 4.45 to 480.76. The average share was down 41 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,815.902, down 74.201, or 0.83 percent.
